eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent model consensus and official agency guidance point to a post-heatwave cooldown setting up a maximum around 26–27 °C in London on 15 August 2026.** After an intense spell that produced a provisional 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens earlier in the week, a thundery breakdown and northerly flow are bringing fresher maritime air across southern England. The Met Office explicitly forecasts a 27 °C daytime maximum for Saturday, while BBC Weather guidance centers on 26 °C; these small differences arise mainly from the precise timing of any residual cloud or light showers and the strength of the north-westerly breeze, which can suppress the peak by 1 °C.

Ensemble output from both ECMWF and GFS shows tight clustering in the mid- to upper-20s, with limited spread reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and any late-day convective development. Historical climatology for mid-August places the long-term average maximum near 22–23 °C, so the current setup remains above normal but far below the preceding heatwave values. With resolution hinging on the official recorded high (typically the highest hourly or synoptic observation at a designated London station), traders are weighting the two leading bins almost equally because forecast error margins of ±1 °C are common at this range and the latest runs continue to straddle the 26–27 °C threshold.

Official guidance from the India Meteorological Department highlights a depression-driven moisture surge favoring scattered thundershowers and increased cloud cover, which limits daytime heating and keeps highs near seasonal norms of 31–33°C. Model consensus shows modest differences in rainfall timing and intensity, directly affecting surface temperatures via evaporative cooling and reduced solar insolation. Historical August records indicate that even brief clear spells can push readings 1–2°C higher, while heavier showers suppress them, explaining the tight clustering around these two outcomes and the lower odds assigned to 35°C or above. Updated short-range model runs and IMD bulletins expected later today will likely refine the exact peak.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Hong Kong Observatory and international sources project a maximum temperature of 31–33 °C for August 15 under typical late-summer conditions of high humidity, light southerly flow, and scattered afternoon showers or thunderstorms. These convective patterns often limit peak heating while allowing brief urban heat-island spikes near official recording stations. Current guidance clusters most likely highs near 32 °C, with limited upside risk from clearer breaks or stronger insolation. Seasonal outlooks already indicate normal-to-above-normal temperatures for the month, consistent with the market’s concentration of probability on 31 °C (43.5 %) and 32 °C (31.0 %), while lower or higher thresholds remain improbable absent an unexpected shift in steering flow or cloud cover. Updated short-range model runs and the next official HKO bulletin are the key near-term catalysts that could refine these implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Singapore's tropical climate under prevailing Southwest Monsoon conditions typically produces daytime maxima near the long-term August average of 31°C, yet recent NEA outlooks highlight drier air and reduced cloud cover supporting readings of 33–34°C through mid-month. Official forecasts for August 15 from sources including the Meteorological Service Singapore, BBC Weather, and AccuWeather converge on a high of 32–33°C, with isolated thundery showers or increased humidity potentially limiting peaks to 31°C. These variables create the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 32°C (58%) and 33°C (22%), reflecting trader assessment of model consensus, historical variability, and the absence of stronger warming signals such as an intensifying El Niño influence. Updated 24-hour guidance and any late adjustments to convective activity will remain key near-term drivers.
